# Test suites that CI runs in the `integration` job, against a real Postgres.
#
# These are the second half of #7. Every suite below was measured twice, once
# against the unroutable placeholder the `static` job uses and once against a
# real PostgreSQL 16: each one FAILS without a database and PASSES with one.
# That is the whole entry requirement, and it is why they cannot live in
# `static` and could never have passed there.
#
# To re-verify this list, or to check a suite before adding one:
#
#   # must FAIL
#   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://ci:ci@127.0.0.1:1/unused \
#   TEST_DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_URL DIRECT_URL=$DATABASE_URL \
#   JWT_SECRET=ci-not-a-real-secret npx jest --runTestsByPath <path> --ci
#
#   # must PASS
#   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/backenly_test \
#   TEST_DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_URL DIRECT_URL=$DATABASE_URL \
#   JWT_SECRET=ci-not-a-real-secret npx jest --runTestsByPath <path> --ci
#
# A suite that passes BOTH ways belongs in database-free-suites.txt instead —
# putting it here would burn a Postgres service container to prove nothing.
#
# Suites that fail even WITH a database are deliberately not here. They are
# listed, with the measured reason, in suites-not-in-ci.txt. Adding a known-red
# suite to a blocking job is how CI became permanently red before (see the note
# on `tests/core` in ci.yml); a red that is always red carries no information.

__tests__/architecture-hardening.test.ts
__tests__/pointer-swap-concurrency.test.ts
__tests__/retry-logic.test.ts
tests/bench/ai-function-db-casts.spec.ts
tests/bench/build-lock-advisory.spec.ts
tests/bench/infra-intelligence-catalog.spec.ts
tests/bench/prisma-uuid-binding.spec.ts
tests/build-runs/build-run-service.test.ts
tests/build-runs/hydration.test.ts
tests/integration/mcp-oauth-flow.spec.ts

# Added 2026-09-04 by the suite-accounting reconciliation. Same measurement as
# every entry above: each FAILS against the unroutable placeholder and PASSES
# against a real PostgreSQL (41/41, 8/8, 12/12 respectively, run individually).
# They guard the billing cancellation and grace lifecycle, project data deletion
# and the purge outbox, all shipped in the last four commits, and belonged to no
# manifest.
__tests__/billing/cancellation-and-grace.test.ts
__tests__/projects/deletion-transaction.test.ts
__tests__/projects/purge-outbox.test.ts

# The ProjectResolver regression matrix (commit 2). Pins the behaviour the ~70
# authorization call sites are being migrated TO, before they are migrated, so
# the migration cannot quietly redefine it. Measured the same way as everything
# above: fails against the unroutable placeholder, passes against a real
# PostgreSQL. Every assertion lives in a `where` clause, which is exactly what a
# mocked client cannot model.
__tests__/auth/project-resolver.test.ts

# The tenant-isolation adapter (commit 2b). withTenantIsolation -> requireProjectId
# -> getCurrentProjectId is now the single decision point for 36 route files, so
# its contract is pinned directly and then again through a real route. Needs a
# database and real signed sessions: the defect lived in a `where` clause and an
# auth branch, neither of which a mocked client models.
__tests__/auth/tenant-isolation-adapter.test.ts

# Representative authorization matrix for app/api/projects/[id]/** (commit 2c).
# One route per authentication pattern rather than 35 near-identical tests,
# because the authorization decision is now identical across the family and only
# the plumbing differs. Asserts the 404-for-both behaviour is preserved, so
# migrating authorization did not start leaking project existence.
__tests__/auth/project-routes-authorization.test.ts

# Project deletion (commit 2c-2b). The only destructive operation the
# authorization migration WIDENS: DELETE /api/projects/[id] was owner-only and
# is now reachable by an organization ADMIN. It drops every workspace schema the
# project owns and there is no undo, so the VIEWER/DEVELOPER/ADMIN/OWNER matrix
# gets its own suite rather than being folded into the general route tests.
__tests__/auth/project-delete-authorization.test.ts

# Single-tenant bootstrap (commit 3). Runs the real script against a database it
# creates and drops, because everything worth asserting is a side effect on
# Postgres: a schema that exists, a row that was not duplicated, a refusal that
# happened before anything was written. It cannot share this job's database:
# bootstrap counts projects globally and the shared one holds many, which is
# itself asserted as the incompatible-database case.
__tests__/bootstrap/single-tenant-bootstrap.test.ts

# The self-hosted single-account claim (commit 3 follow-up). The pre-flight
# check in assertSignupAllowed runs ~50 lines before the insert, so it cannot be
# the enforcement: two concurrent first signups would both read zero accounts.
# The claim is made inside the inserting transaction behind an advisory lock,
# and this asserts it under genuine concurrency rather than in sequence.
__tests__/auth/first-account-claim.test.ts

# setup-postgrest-roles idempotency (commit 3 follow-up). --apply used to run
# ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD unconditionally with a fresh random password, so
# re-running a command documented as repeatable rotated the credential a live
# PostgREST authenticates with. Roles are CLUSTER-WIDE, so this suite uses a
# throwaway authenticator and its own database.
__tests__/bootstrap/postgrest-roles-idempotency.test.ts

# Single-tenant ownership: THE project is created before anyone signs up, so it
# starts owner-less and must adopt the first operator. Runs the real script
# against its own database, because the failure was a state the database was
# allowed to sit in.
__tests__/bootstrap/single-tenant-ownership.test.ts
